commit_files() correctly reports a merge commit's changed files as its diff against its FIRST PARENT (not the empty result plain diff-tree gives a merge, and not the combined/-m diff, which pulls in the union against every parent). Proven by test_commit_files_uses_first_parent_diff_for_a_merge_commit, and directly re-verified against this repo's own live history: commit_files() on a real merge commit on main (07f82d1d45d9...) now returns exactly the two reviews/51/*.json files it actually changed, where before this fix it returned [].

resolve_reviewable_head() walks PAST a merge commit whose first-parent diff touches only reviews/ or proof/ files, exactly like it already skips an ordinary record-only commit -- the live staling bug this fix addresses. Proven by test_reviewable_head_skips_a_merge_that_only_brought_in_review_records.

A merge must never be able to smuggle real content past the review requirement by also carrying a reviews/ file alongside it -- resolve_reviewable_head() must NOT skip a merge whose first-parent diff touches real content too. Proven by test_reviewable_head_does_not_skip_a_merge_carrying_real_content_too.

A merge with a genuinely empty first-parent diff (e.g. an -s ours no-op merge) is treated as record-only/skippable, distinct from an ordinary empty (non-merge) commit which stays NOT record-only -- both behaviors proven and reasoned about explicitly in code comments. Proven by test_is_record_only_commit_true_for_a_merge_with_empty_first_parent_diff and test_is_record_only_commit_still_false_for_an_ordinary_empty_commit.

commit_files() reporting a merge's real first-parent diff must not feed check_lanes' per-file lane-OWNERSHIP check (only the shared-path/review-freshness determination) -- a merge did not personally author files it brings in from its second parent. Proven by test_check_lanes_merge_with_out_of_lane_file_does_not_fail_lane_ownership (which also pins that commit_files itself still reports the file, so the fix hides it from ownership checking only) -- a second, independently found consequence of the merge-commit fix.

The merge lane-ownership exemption is not a blanket amnesty: a non-merge commit that directly touches a file outside the committing agent's lane still fails, unchanged. Proven by test_check_lanes_merge_still_rejects_a_directly_authored_out_of_lane_file.
